name: California

incomeTax.summary: Progressive state income tax from 1% to 13.3% — the highest top marginal rate in the country
incomeTax.note: California's Employment Training Tax and SDI payroll deductions also come out of paychecks, and the 13.3% top bracket applies above $1 million.

laborNote: California sets a high wage floor: the state minimum wage, strict overtime rules, and mandatory pay-range disclosure in job postings (SB 1162) all push published salaries upward.

name: Texas

incomeTax.summary: No state income tax — Texas is one of nine states with zero tax on wages
incomeTax.note: Texas funds government largely through property and sales taxes, so homeowners face property tax rates among the highest in the nation (averaging around 1.6%).

laborNote: Texas is a right-to-work state with no state minimum wage above the federal floor, so pay is driven almost entirely by market demand rather than mandates — which favors in-demand skilled roles.

name: Florida

incomeTax.summary: No state income tax — wages are only subject to federal tax
incomeTax.note: Florida's constitution prohibits a personal income tax, but fast-rising home insurance premiums and housing costs offset some of that advantage.

laborNote: Florida's minimum wage is stepping up to $15 by constitutional amendment, compressing pay at the low end, while rapid population growth keeps demand high for healthcare and construction workers.

name: New York

incomeTax.summary: Progressive state income tax from 4% to 10.9%, plus a separate New York City income tax of up to 3.876% for city residents
incomeTax.note: Combined state and city taxes make NYC one of the highest-tax places to earn a paycheck in the U.S., though salaries upstate face only the state tax.

laborNote: New York requires salary ranges in job postings statewide and has strong public-sector unions, which lifts published pay for teachers, police, and trades well above national schedules.

name: Washington

incomeTax.summary: No state income tax on wages — though Washington levies a 7% capital gains tax above an inflation-indexed threshold
incomeTax.note: Washington pairs zero wage tax with one of the highest state minimum wages in the country, and Seattle sets its own even higher city minimum.

laborNote: Washington's pay transparency law requires salary ranges in every job posting, and the concentration of tech headquarters around Seattle pulls average wages up across many occupations, not just software.
